This market will resolve based on the highest temperature recorded in the 'Daily Observations' table on Weather Underground, not the figure displayed in the 'Day High & Low' summary section; in the event of any discrepancy between the two, the Daily Observations table shall be the primary resolution source not the Day High & Low section.

This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature recorded at the London City Airport Station in degrees Celsius on 11 Aug '26.

The resolution source for this market will be information from Wunderground, specifically the highest temperature recorded for all times on this day for the London City Airport Station, available here: https://www.wunderground.com/history/daily/gb/london/EGLC.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the gear icon next to the search bar and switch the Temperature setting between °F and °C.

This market can not resolve until the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

eventMetadata.context_description: Recent forecasts from the Met Office and other models indicate a high-pressure system bringing mostly sunny conditions to London on August 11, 2026, supporting daytime maxima near 25–26°C under light winds and minimal cloud cover. This setup favors radiative warming during peak solar hours, though urban heat island effects and any late-day sea breezes from the Thames could cap the exact peak. Trader consensus clustering on 24–25°C reflects model spread in boundary-layer mixing and slight timing differences in any frontal approaches, with historical August averages around 22°C providing context for the elevated but not extreme outlook. eventMetadata.context_description: A strong cold front and upper trough have recently swept across the Western Cape, advecting cooler maritime air with elevated winds and increased cloud cover that limit daytime heating in Cape Town. Ensemble forecasts and South African Weather Service guidance converge on a maximum near the climatological August average of 18°C, positioning 19°C as the mode with 54.5% implied probability while capping upside potential at 20°C (23%). Historical analogs for post-frontal August days rarely exceed 20–21°C under similar steering patterns, and limited recovery expected before August 11 reinforces the tight distribution around these outcomes. Updated model runs ahead of final observations could shift sentiment if onshore flow moderates further.

This setup stems from a mid-level trough and associated frontal activity shifting across western Russia, reducing solar insolation during peak afternoon hours and enhancing evaporative cooling from moist surfaces. The tight spread between 17°C and 18°C arises from minor uncertainties in exact cloud timing, boundary-layer mixing, and local advection; a slightly earlier frontal passage or thicker cloud deck would favor 17°C, while clearer breaks or stronger southerly flow could push toward 19°C. Official short-range guidance from monitoring agencies shows low probability of reaching 20°C or higher given the current synoptic pattern, keeping those outcomes in single digits. Updated model cycles and afternoon observations over the next 24–48 hours will refine the peak value ahead of market resolution.

**Trader sentiment for Amsterdam's peak temperature on August 12, 2026, centers on 26–28°C, with 27°C leading at 36.5% implied probability and 28°C close behind at 29.5%.** These odds reflect short-range ensemble forecasts from models such as ECMWF and GFS, which show a warm, mostly dry high-pressure pattern over the Netherlands amid an above-average early-August spell.

Primary drivers include southerly or easterly advection of continental air under clear or partly cloudy skies, moderate insolation near the summer solstice peak, and limited cloud cover or precipitation that would otherwise suppress daytime heating. Boundary-layer mixing and a modest urban heat-island effect in Amsterdam add roughly 1°C locally. Small differences in forecast timing of any weak front, wind speed, or afternoon cloud build-up create the narrow spread between 26°C and 28°C; ensembles currently place the most likely maximum near 27°C.

Recent model updates through August 10 have kept probabilities tightly clustered, with only modest upward revisions for 28–29°C if clearer skies prevail. Resolution hinges on the official KNMI observation at the Amsterdam station, so traders monitor the latest 48-hour runs and any shifts in 2-meter temperature guidance.
